query: Why do expense decline rates differ across departments?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Type of expense (hardware/travel/software) plausibly affects both what departments purchase (varies by department) and the likelihood of decline (different approval scrutiny). Common cause of department-composition and outcome.

per_column.name: device_form_factor
per_column.rationale: Finer-grained item type; correlates with department mix and with decline likelihood (expensive servers vs peripherals). Plausible common cause, though partly redundant with asset_category_type.

per_column.name: entry_origin
per_column.rationale: Manual vs auto-generated entry is a candidate cause: manual entries may be declined more often due to error/incompleteness. This is a plausible treatment whose effect on decline rate could be attributed.

per_column.name: vendor_brand
per_column.rationale: Vendor may relate to which department buys and to approval outcome (approved vendor lists), so a plausible common cause, though effect is weaker.

per_column.name: is_travel_related
per_column.rationale: Travel status affects department composition and decline propensity (travel policies stricter). Overlaps with asset_category_type.

per_column.name: ci_identifier_quality
per_column.rationale: Quality/legibility of the CI identifier plausibly affects reviewability (decline) and may vary by department practices. Weak but plausible common cause.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: Completeness of record (source id present) may drive decline and vary by department entry process. Could also be treated as treatment; treated here as a data-quality common cause.

per_column.name: recurring_submitter
per_column.rationale: Whether the submitter is recurring may affect both submission patterns (concentrated in some departments) and decline likelihood (familiarity with policy). Plausible common cause.

judge.rationale: The query names only the outcome (decline rate variation) and the grouping (department); no treatment or confounders are named, so all surfaced variables are query-independent, which is the capability under test. entry_origin (manual vs auto) is the clearest candidate TREATMENT whose effect on decline could be attributed. Several added columns (asset_category_type, is_travel_related, has_source_id, recurring_submitter) are plausible common causes of both what a department submits and whether it is declined, so they function as genuine confounders. However quality is only moderate: many columns describe item/asset attributes that are strongly redundant with each other, and their status as common causes of the treatment (manual entry) is weak — several read more as parallel candidate causes or descriptive attributes than as classical confounders adjusting a specific treatment-outcome pair. No clear mediators or colliders are labelled as confounders, but the set is skewed toward item-type descriptors rather than variables that jointly cause the manual-entry treatment and the decline outcome.
